stage: phase B result layer. This file states an outcome; it does not amend the pre-registration or the tolerance, and neither of those was touched by the commit that adds it
recomputation_note: every DERIVED quantity below -- reaction time, stopping distance, the prediction, the residual, the gate 2 verdict, the clearance, the hazard classification and every summary statistic -- was recomputed from phase-b-raw-held.json and the frozen artifacts by tools/verify_external_phase_b.py. The collaborator's own summary, report and classified table were read only to check that they agreed, and are not the source of a derived value here
taken_as_given_from_the_external_party: the measured evidence itself (per-trial positions, ticks and stop velocities) and the provenance around it (simulator identity and version, the configuration, and the statement that the run was not repeated after the tolerance was frozen). This repository cannot derive those from anything it holds; it verifies their digests and recomputes everything downstream of them

ordering.2_phase_a_metadata_disclosed: simulator, integrator, solver, stop semantics, timing representation and per-trial timing ticks, with every measured distance withheld
ordering.4_phase_b_disclosed: the already-held measured outputs were released only after the tolerance commit existed
ordering.5_this_result: evaluates already-held data against an already-frozen criterion
ordering.what_git_history_establishes: the ordering of the public commits: the pre-registration at cabace5a2c02da4ebbef3494b54ce87b324c348f, the tolerance freeze at 1490238eb35e4b4dfce115c428b7d5907eadf58a, and this result layer after both
ordering.what_git_history_does_not_establish: that phase A was disclosed between the first two, or that phase B was released only after the tolerance freeze. Those are documented by the preserved external evidence and correspondence rather than by git history alone. Committing the phase A timing file puts the disclosed metadata on the public record here; the timing of the phase B release rests on the external party's account

external_simulator.name: OmniSim
external_simulator.physics_runtime: Newton 1.5.0 with MuJoCo 3.11.0 on the deterministic CPU mj_step path
external_simulator.provenance: declared in phase A. The external party states that the configuration was unchanged for phase B and that the run was not repeated after the tolerance was frozen; that is their statement, not something this repository can verify from the evidence

phase_a_continuity.evidence_provenance: the original phase A timing file exactly as received before phase B existed, taken byte for byte from pickcell_phase_a.zip. It was not regenerated or reserialised, and its digest was recomputed from those bytes
phase_a_continuity.method: the 25 phase B trials are compared field by field against the 25 phase A timing rows
phase_a_continuity.comparison_semantics: type-sensitive comparison of parsed values. Integer and floating-point types must remain the same, and floating-point values are compared using their canonical Python representation, so different parsed binary64 values are rejected and cases such as -0.0 versus 0.0 remain distinguishable. This is a semantic value-continuity check, not a claim that the numeric tokens have byte-identical textual spelling: two decimal spellings that parse to the same binary64 compare equal here
phase_a_continuity.byte_level_preservation_established_sepa: the pinned SHA-256 digests of the received evidence files and the .gitattributes -text rules that stop git normalising them
phase_a_continuity.result: every phase A timing field is identical in phase B. Phase B adds only the eight fields that were withheld and alters none of the timing that was already public
phase_a_continuity.run_by: tools/verify_external_phase_b.py, on every CI run, from committed evidence alone
phase_a_continuity.what_this_proves: that the phase B evidence preserves the phase A-disclosed timing metadata exactly under the verifier's comparison semantics. It would detect a rerun or replacement only if that operation changed one of those committed fields
phase_a_continuity.what_this_does_not_prove: that no rerun occurred. Identical timing metadata alone cannot distinguish a preserved run from a deterministic rerun under identical conditions. The collaborator's no-rerun statement therefore remains provenance supplied by the external party, while the field-by-field comparison independently establishes continuity of the disclosed metadata
phase_a_continuity.why_it_matters: phase A was published while every measured distance was still withheld, so its timing was on the record before the results were. Committing the phase A file is what makes the comparison repeatable by a third party rather than an assertion about something done once on a maintainer's machine

trial_identities: the exact Cartesian product of the frozen polling intervals 10, 25, 50, 100 and 200 ms with phase indices 1 to 5. No duplicates, none missing, none added
gate_1_note: semantic agreement was already establishable from the phase A world file and controller and is unchanged by phase B: one translational degree of freedom along +x, the frozen initial state, the frozen segment durations and jerks, no gravity along the travel axis, no contact, a non-interacting hazard plane, and velocity held constant through the reaction interval
gate_2_rule: abs(stopping_distance_m - (2.0 * T + 0.450)) <= delta_m, per trial, evaluated at that trial's own T

diagnostic_analysis.status: descriptive only. Gate 2 remains the frozen absolute-residual rule and was not tightened because the results came in well inside it
diagnostic_analysis.residual_sign: negative in all 25 trials, as predicted before disclosure. The simulated stop travels about 1 mm less than the continuous prediction

scatter_bounded_at_the_float32_scale.provenance: INDEPENDENTLY CHECKABLE from the committed evidence, and rechecked from it
scatter_bounded_at_the_float32_scale.statement: the committed measurements show that the observed scatter is bounded at the scale expected from float32 representation: all 50 stored position values and all 25 final stop velocities are exactly representable in single precision, and every departure from the pre-registered -1 mm diagnostic expectation is below the float32 spacing at the corresponding absolute coordinate
scatter_bounded_at_the_float32_scale.why_the_spacing_grows: the axis is not reset between trials, so the absolute coordinate grows across the ladder and its representation step grows with it. That is also one reason the classification is on stopping distance rather than on the absolute coordinate

float32_mechanism_statement.provenance: REPORTED_BY_SIMULATOR. External simulator provenance supplied by OmniLink, not derivable from the committed evidence
float32_mechanism_statement.statement: OmniLink states that the simulator state is carried in single precision before it reaches the controller, which makes float32 quantization an operative mechanism in the disclosed run rather than only a compatible explanation
float32_mechanism_statement.boundary: the representability and ULP comparisons above stand on the committed evidence alone. This mechanism statement does not, and is recorded as the external party's account

hazard_classification.classified_quantity: stopping_distance_m, the distance travelled from t_hazard_assertion to rest
hazard_classification.not_classified_on: stop_position_m, which is an absolute world coordinate on an axis that is not reset between trials and reaches about 15.6 m

crossing_sanity_check.status: sanity check only. The frozen classification is on stopping distance and was not replaced by a reaction-time gate
crossing_sanity_check.observation: both CROSSED trials sit well beyond that boundary at T = 0.152 s and T = 0.181 s, and every CLEAR trial sits below it, the nearest being the 200 ms phase 4 trial at T = 0.105 s. No trial lands near the band, which is why no trial is INDETERMINATE

stop_semantics_check.result: every trial came to rest far inside the declared threshold
stop_semantics_check.braking_duration_check: in all 25 trials the stop tick is exactly 450 ticks after the profile start tick, matching the frozen 0.450 s braking profile at the 1 ms timestep

timing_check.T_definition: T = t_profile_start_tick - t_hazard_assertion_tick, times the 1 ms timestep

simulator_build_reproduction_limit.provenance: REPORTED_BY_SIMULATOR. OmniLink's account of their current build, not something this repository reproduced or can check
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.reported: the same frozen world and controller no longer complete the ladder on OmniLink's current build. The axis does not reach the 2.0 m/s initial condition inside the controller's spin-up allowance, so the run aborts on that pre-condition rather than emitting a different set of stopping distances. OmniLink reports the behaviour as repeatable
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.fails_before_any_new_output: the reported failure occurs at the initial-condition pre-condition, before a new stopping distance is produced. It is the absence of a result, not a different result
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.committed_evidence_unaffected: the published phase B evidence is immutable and every derived quantity here recomputes from those committed bytes with no simulator involved. Nothing in this result depends on re-executing the simulation
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.reproduction_of_the_simulator_execution: reproduction of the published simulator execution is established for the build and environment disclosed in phase A -- OmniSim 8.3.0 at cdfb678ca4f687eb56742af3509083e02ee149e6, Newton 1.5.0, MuJoCo 3.11.0 on the deterministic CPU mj_step path. OmniLink reports that their current build is not a drop-in reproduction target because it aborts at the initial-condition precondition before emitting stopping-distance results
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.what_that_does_not_establish: that no other build could reproduce the run. It establishes that the published result is pinned to, and should be interpreted against, the phase A-disclosed simulator and build provenance
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.does_not_invalidate_the_result: this changes no measurement, no residual, no gate outcome, no tolerance and no classification. Nothing was reclassified because of it
simulator_build_reproduction_limit.why_it_matters: it is the argument for pinning simulator and build provenance in the pre-registration. A result whose numbers recompute from committed bytes, and whose execution is pinned to a named build, keeps its meaning when the upstream toolchain moves

velocity_trace_note: the external run recorded a final stop velocity per trial but captured no time-series velocity trace, and none was reconstructed afterwards. This makes the optional diagnostic trace comparison unavailable. It is missing diagnostic evidence, not a failure of gate 1 or gate 2, neither of which ever depended on it

scope.what_this_establishes: that an independent simulator, given the same reaction time and the same commanded braking law, produces a stopping distance consistent with this repository's analytical prediction to within a tolerance frozen before the numbers were seen
what_this_does_not_establish: this repository's own measured reaction times, which a simulated polling model does not reproduce or confirm
scope.primary_result: stopping distance. Clearance and crossing are arithmetic against the frozen plane, not separate independent findings

verifier.note: recomputes every derived quantity from the raw held measurement and the frozen artifacts, checks phase A to phase B continuity from the committed phase A timing file, then fails if this summary, the compact table, the pinned digests or the manifests disagree

external_archive_contents.note: the full inventory of the archive as received, so a reader can verify the original even though only two of its files are committed here. The frozen_repository_package entries are the collaborator's copies of files already in this repository and are byte-identical to them

retention_rationale.zip_not_committed: the archive itself is not committed. Every file it contains is listed below with its size and SHA-256, so the original remains verifiable by anyone who obtains it
retention_rationale.canonical_evidence: phase-b-raw-held.json is the canonical raw measurement evidence. Every derived quantity in this result is recomputed from it, and nothing else in the archive can stand in for it
retention_rationale.csv_is_a_cross_format_check: phase-b-trials.csv is semantically derivable from the raw trials, so retaining it is not strictly necessary to reproduce the result. Its original bytes are kept because it is an independently received serialisation of the same trials, which lets the verifier check the two representations against each other as well as against recomputation. The raw JSON and the CSV therefore encode overlapping trial information by design
retention_rationale.omitted_as_derivable: the collaborator's classified table, report and summary are values the verifier recomputes from the raw measurement, and the frozen_repository_package files are copies of artifacts already committed here. Those are inventoried by digest rather than duplicated in full

committed_in_this_repository.role: independently received serialisation of the same trials, retained as a cross-format consistency check
